::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
SMIC's Beijing expansion JV (中芯京城, 54.04% SMIC-owned), targeting 100,000 wafers/month of 12-inch, 28nm-and-above capacity in the Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area.
:::

**Chinese name:** 中芯京城 (Zhōngxīn Jīngchéng)

## What does this facility make?

12-inch (300mm) wafers at 28nm and more mature nodes for foundry customers.

## Why does it matter?

Reported investment figures vary slightly by source — $7.6 billion (Yicai) and $7.7 billion / RMB 49.7 billion (CnTechPost) — likely the same commitment described at slightly different points or currency conversions; both are given here since no source explicitly reconciles them. Phase 1 was already in use by late 2023; a separate Phase 2 land deal (early 2026) was reported at a total project investment of no less than ¥50 billion (¥40 billion in fixed-asset investment), targeting an annual output value of at least ¥6 billion once fully ramped.

## Project Timeline

- **Feb 2021** — Development of the $7.6-7.7 billion Beijing fab (SMIC Jingcheng) begins; first phase targeted for completion by 2024
- **Nov 2023** — Phase 1 confirmed in use, per Beijing E-Town Investment Holding disclosure
- **Jan 2025** — Tongzhou district officials commit to fully completing Phase 2's main structure, with equipment installation underway
